diagnosis.primary_fault: Cracked LCD / OLED Display Panel (Physical Impact)
supporting_evidence: Reported symptoms directly match indicator terms: crack
safe_checks: 1. Connect laptop to an external monitor via HDMI to verify that GPU and motherboard boot successfully.
2. If external monitor displays the OS, the core system is healthy and only the screen panel requires replacement.
advanced_steps: 1. Disconnect AC charger and internal battery.
2. Remove the screen bezel frame using a plastic pry tool.
3. Unscrew LCD panel mounting brackets and note the panel part number sticker on the back (e.g. NV156FHM-N48).
4. Unclip the 30-pin or 40-pin eDP video connector gently.
5. Install the replacement panel, reconnect eDP cable firmly, test before snapping bezel back.
safety_instructions: Disconnect the battery and AC charger before touching the eDP display cable to avoid blowing the motherboard backlight fuse.
